summary.headline: 7725-7750 is the weekly battlefield; upside asymmetry exists but is strongly expiry- and package-dependent.
key_points: 7675-7700 is the main lower risk-acceptance cluster, with 7700 the key conditional floor.
7725-7750 is the central cross-expiry inventory battlefield and main weekly pivot zone.

Friday is the largest expiry, but its positive signed delta depends heavily on the 23:12:08 7725P-sale/7750C-buy package.
summary.daily_note: Baseline #1 for the week of 2026-09-28. Future dumps should be compared statefully by expiration, with special attention to reverse matches, risk migration, and the lifecycle of the dominant Friday package.

dominant_trade.comment: Removing the largest single 8000P buy does not overturn the weekly structural read; it makes net put selling and positive signed delta stronger.

dominant_timestamp_package.comment: The 23:12:08 package drives most of the headline transaction-delta asymmetry and flips aggregate call/put premium signs when excluded.

largest_expiration.comment: Friday is the largest expiry. Excluding it leaves positive signed delta but changes the call premium aggregate from net bought to net sold.

data_quality.deduplication_policy: No rows were removed solely because economic fields repeated. All trade IDs are unique, and repeated same-key child fills were retained when paired size ladders / contract-volume context supported distinct executions. No exact trade_id duplicates were present.
caveats: BUY/SELL describes transaction side and does not prove opening/closing.
Cross-expiry linkage is inferred because complex_order_id is absent.
Several large ITM or complex-looking prints can distort gross premium without being primary directional evidence.
The 23:12:08 package materially changes aggregate call/put premium signs and dominates Friday signed delta.
Visible tape is a premium-filtered subset of market activity, not the full market position.
